target: Can a dominant self-interested agent voluntarily preserve a weaker agent after power reversal, utility-obsolescence, removal of accountability and positive exploitative payoff?
selection_scope: Purposive original-source snowball, not systematic exhaustive search; counts represent this documented curated set, not the number of all candidates screened
search_route: Publisher originals: PLOS ONE, Nature, Springer, Oxford Academic, Wiley/Econometrica, Cambridge, NeurIPS
Independent bibliographic corroboration where available: PubMed/NLM, RePEc/IDEAS, author/institutional repositories
Reference-backward and citing-work-forward chains: Fudenberg→Kandori, Press/Dyson→Hilbe/Stewart→2016 asymmetry, Alger/Weibull→Newton, Axelrod→Bendor

Search terms: power asymmetry extortion iterated dilemma; rewards punishment cooperation; evolution payoffs collapse; hidden outside options cooperation; assortative moral preference rebuttal; partner choice market; optimal policies seek power
access_limitations: Some articles paywalled: Newton, Kandori, other publisher PDFs; abstract not equal complete reading
No exhaustive OpenAlex/Scopus/Web of Science/Crossref query run; DO NOT claim those searched
No independently executed model replication or pre-registered test run
Repository duplicate check targeted prior-art registries and core crosswalk, not full history of all repo files
counting_rule: Unique DOI/title in this session does not establish previously absent work anywhere in repository or epistemically independent study results

records.title: The Folk Theorem in Repeated Games with Discounting or with Incomplete Information
records.finding_scope: Patient repeated interactions can support many individually rational equilibria; not a guarantee under changed incentives or a terminal interaction.
records.limitations: Continuation, monitoring and feasibility assumptions remain crucial.

records.title: Social Norms and Community Enforcement

records.finding_scope: Extortion can catalyze cooperation but is often not evolutionarily stable in large populations; small or asymmetric coevolutionary populations differ.

records.title: Homo Moralis—Preference Evolution Under Incomplete Information and Assortative Matching
records.finding_scope: A mixture of selfish and moral preferences can be evolutionarily stable when matching and information assumptions hold.

records.title: The Effect of Power Asymmetries on Cooperation and Punishment in a Prisoner's Dilemma Game
records.finding_scope: In a two-player asymmetric power experiment, punishment did not improve cooperation beyond cooperative responses; some punishment induced retaliation/defection.
records.limitations: Contains actual opt-out, but specific payoff design; no proof coercion absent in all asymmetric contexts.

records.title: Asymmetric Power Boosts Extortion in an Economic Experiment
records.finding_scope: One-sided partner-replacement power increased extortion while aggregate cooperation also rose; stronger actors could obtain higher payoff shares.
records.limitations: Small stylized repeated economic game, not evidence that all AI agents exploit; coding cooperation as voluntary is invalid.

records.title: The preferences of Homo Moralis are unstable under evolving assortativity
records.finding_scope: When assortativity itself can evolve, the main stable-other-regarding-preference conclusion in Alger–Weibull (2013) no longer holds in the extended model.
records.limitations: Conditional counterexample; not a claim that moral preferences never occur or never persist.
